authoring.note: A large windowless hall where a Frame and its pilot are measured against each other. Quiet, instrumented, and booked by the hour.

lore.summary: A large, deliberately windowless hall where a Frame and the person who pilots it are measured against one another. Resonance is read here: what a pilot can currently be trusted to do, established by instrument rather than by opinion, and written down. Sessions are booked by the hour and run to a schedule the whole strip works around. The hall is quiet in a way no other building on this strip is, and the quiet is structural -- the readings are delicate, so the Armour Shop's heaviest work is timetabled around the Calibration Hall's day rather than the other way about.
lore.playerFacing: A floor big enough to stand a Frame on, ringed by instrument cabinets and a gallery of people watching dials rather than watching you. Nobody raises their voice. Every number that comes off the session is read aloud once, written down twice, and initialled by somebody who was in the room.
lore.gmOnly:
Use this as the place where Resonance stops being a number on a sheet and becomes a thing done to a character in a room full of people, on a schedule they do not control.

Deliberately NOT decided here: whether anything in this building can reduce Bleed. That is open-questions.json#bleed-recovery-sinks and it is Ingram's call -- the hall is written as measurement only, so it stays usable whichever way that question lands. Do not let a session here quietly become a Bleed sink at the table before it has been decided properly.

The readings are institutional facts, not private ones. Anything measured here is written down, and a pilot who wants a number kept quiet is asking for something the building is not built to do.

hooks: A pilot's reading comes back different from the last one and nobody in the gallery will say in front of them whether different is good.
The hall's schedule is quietly rearranged to fit somebody in, which means somebody else has been bumped, and the bumped party finds out from the board rather than from a person.
activities: Sit a calibration session and be measured, with an audience.
Read the day's board and work out from the bookings alone what the Directorate is planning.
Ask the staff what a number actually means and find out how much they are allowed to tell you.
